subsystems.name: Roadside sensing unit
subsystems.role: captures real-time traffic at each intersection.

subsystems.name: Edge computing node
subsystems.role: runs AI models locally to avoid cloud latency.

subsystems.name: Communication mesh
subsystems.role: shares data between intersections and vehicles.

subsystems.name: Signal control interface
subsystems.role: translates decisions into safe signal phases.

subsystems.name: Distributed optimization engine
parts: reinforcement learning or model predictive control

buildSteps.title: Survey and instrument intersections
buildSteps.detail: Install cameras, radar and edge computers on poles at selected crossings, with local power and network links.

buildSteps.title: Train perception models
buildSteps.detail: Collect and label local video and sensor data, then train models to detect and track cars, bicycles and pedestrians.

buildSteps.title: Deploy edge inference
buildSteps.detail: Optimize models to run in milliseconds on low-power edge hardware, testing under rain, glare and night conditions.

buildSteps.title: Establish mesh communication
buildSteps.detail: Configure wireless mesh or fiber links between intersections, measuring latency and reliability over days of operation.

buildSteps.title: Implement distributed control
buildSteps.detail: Develop algorithms that adjust green times and offsets based on local queues and data from neighbouring nodes, with a safe fallback to fixed-time plans.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with signal controllers
buildSteps.detail: Use standard interfaces such as NTCIP to send phase commands to existing traffic signal controllers without replacing them.

buildSteps.title: Simulate and field-test
buildSteps.detail: Validate the mesh in a traffic simulation, then pilot on a real corridor while measuring travel times, stops and emissions.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate and scale
buildSteps.detail: Compare results against fixed-time and centrally controlled signals, then expand the mesh to more intersections if gains hold.

prerequisites.why: needs low-power, high-performance chips that survive heat, cold and vibration in roadside cabinets.
standards like C-V2X exist, but few vehicles on the road are equipped to talk to intersections.
mature for detection and tracking, but still challenged by heavy rain, snow and low sun.
many controllers use proprietary protocols, and standard interfaces like NTCIP are not universally adopted.
shown in simulation and small pilots, but large-scale field validation is still limited.

pathway.milestone: pilots on single corridors with a handful of instrumented intersections
pathway.unlocks: evidence that edge AI can cut delay and emissions compared with fixed-time signals.

pathway.milestone: city-wide mesh coordinating hundreds of intersections
pathway.unlocks: network-level flow optimisation and reduced stop-and-go traffic across districts.

pathway.milestone: integration with connected and autonomous vehicles
pathway.unlocks: cooperative driving where vehicles and signals negotiate safe, smooth crossings.

pathway.milestone: standardised, interoperable edge-AI traffic mesh deployed in many cities
pathway.unlocks: safer, cleaner and more efficient urban mobility at scale.
